sections.Children need 2 doses of varicella vacci: First dose: 12 through 15 months of ageSecond dose: 4 through 6 years of ageOlder children, adolescents, and adults also need 2 doses of varicella vaccine if they are not already immune to chickenpox.Varicella vaccine may be given at the same time as other vaccines. Also, a child between 12 months and 12 years of age might receive varicella vaccine together with MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) vaccine in a single shot, known as MMRV. Your health care provider can give you more information.
sections.Tell your vaccine provider if the person: Has had an allergic reaction after a previous dose of varicella vaccine, or has any severe, life-threatening allergiesIs pregnant or thinks she might be pregnant— pregnant women should not get varicella vaccineHas a weakened immune system, or has a parent, brother, or sister with a history of hereditary or congenital immune system problemsIs taking salicylates (such as aspirin).Has recently had a blood transfusion or received other blood productsHas tuberculosis.Has gotten any other vaccines in the past 4 weeks.In some cases, your health care provider may decide to postpone varicella vaccination until a future visit.People with minor illnesses, such as a cold, may be vaccinated. People who are moderately or severely ill should usually wait until they recover before getting varicella vaccine.Your health care provider can give you more information.
